clue.text: One-sided support for literature

parts.note: a prop standing at one end of a shelf, holding up a row of books from a single side

explanation.definitionFit: A shelf prop placed at the end of a row of volumes keeps them upright from one side only.

clue.text: Attack main site of power station

parts.note: to batter is to attack with blows
the main is a poetic word for the open sea

explanation.surface: Assault the principal location of a power plant.
explanation.walkthrough: BATTERSEA is the London district whose huge brick power station on the Thames is a landmark.
explanation.definitionFit: The south London district on the Thames is famous for its four-chimneyed power station.

clue.text: Nothing able to move fast round it in cloudy conditions

parts.note: O, the figure zero, means nothing

indicators.note: round says the word for speedy goes around it

parts.note: pacy means quick or speedy

explanation.surface: Nothing can speed around in murky weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts IT inside PACY to give PACITY after O.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of transparency, the quality of being cloudy or murky.

clue.text: Early bite from seven eels, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps tells the solver that the letters of these two words may be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A fish nibbles a line early on, perhaps among seven eels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges SEVEN EELS; 'bite' is a snack, not an angler's nibble.
explanation.definitionFit: A British mid-morning snack, taken around eleven o'clock, before lunch.

clue.text: Chief magistrate's conclusions in end do swing outcome

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: conclusions in takes the final letter of each of the next four words

explanation.surface: A senior judge's verdicts finally decide the result.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letters of end, do, swing and outcome give D, O, G, E.
explanation.definitionFit: The elected ruler of the old republics of Venice and Genoa was the chief magistrate.

clue.text: Half of 16 is both round and square

definitions.text: Half of 16 is both round and square

parts.words: Half of 16 is both round and square
parts.note: sixteen ... written in words has this as its second half, and the number ten squared is a round figure as well as a perfect square

explanation.walkthrough: Write 1600 in words and the second of its two words is the answer; that number is also ten times ten, so it is both a round number and a square one.
explanation.definitionFit: Ten times ten is a perfect square and a famously round figure, the number of a century.

clue.text: He did a lady's portrait for two kings

parts.note: Henry is the name of eight English kings
James is the name of English and Scottish kings

explanation.surface: An artist painted a lady on behalf of a pair of monarchs.
explanation.walkthrough: He wrote the novel The Portrait of a Lady; both his names are royal names.
explanation.definitionFit: The American novelist wrote The Portrait of a Lady, published in 1881.

clue.text: Move cautiously, catching nothing in snare

indicators.note: catching says the word for move cautiously holds the next piece inside

parts.note: to nose forward is to move ahead carefully
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Someone creeps up slowly but catches nothing in their trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching' puts O inside NOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A loop of rope that tightens when pulled is used as a trap for animals.

clue.text: Balloted again for rising new guard

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means the word for guard is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a warder is a prison guard

explanation.surface: A fresh guard was voted in again because of promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reverses WARDER to REDRAW in this down clue; N follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Lots or a ballot drawn a second time; draws are held again.

clue.text: Ventured to find ringleader in disturbance

indicators.note: in says the leader's letter goes inside the word for disturbance

parts.note: a dust, as in kicking up a dust, is a row or disturbance
the leader of ring is its first letter, R

explanation.surface: Someone dared to track down the instigator of a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringleader' is the first letter of ring, R, put inside DUST.
explanation.definitionFit: An old past tense of dare: one who durst not was one who dared not.

clue.text: Sort of cycle seen in traffic

explanation.surface: Some kind of bicycle is spotted among the cars.
explanation.definitionFit: The trade cycle is the economic boom-and-bust pattern; to traffic is to buy and sell goods.

clue.text: Contents of magazine now purged, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps tells the solver the letters of these two words may form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: An editor has cleared out a magazine's articles.
explanation.walkthrough: The magazine is an arms store, not a periodical: 'perhaps' rearranges NOW PURGED.
explanation.definitionFit: A powder magazine is a store for explosives, so black powder is what it holds.

clue.text: Left the scene agitated, with no end of panic

indicators.note: with no says a letter is dropped from the word for agitated

parts.note: agitated means excited or worked up

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of panic

explanation.surface: Someone stormed off in a flustered state, but without actually panicking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' gives C, the last letter of panic, and 'with no' removes it from EXCITED.
explanation.definitionFit: To exit is to go out, as an actor goes off stage in a script's direction.

clue.text: Model found to be lacking original parts

parts.note: a model or pattern is a type
to found metal is to cast it in a mould

explanation.surface: A fashion model is discovered to have no new roles on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' is not the past of find but the foundry verb: founding metal means casting it.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor stuck playing the same kind of role over and over is never given fresh characters.

clue.text: Entrepreneur has to surpass it with a catalogue

parts.note: to cap something is to outdo or surpass it
a list is a catalogue

explanation.surface: A businessman must outdo it by publishing a catalogue.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who invests capital in business enterprise for profit.

clue.text: Eyesores, in a way? That's right .

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
yes is the word for agreeing that something is right

explanation.surface: Ugly sights are, in some sense, exactly what is being described.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Eyesores' as eye sores: little inflamed swellings on an eyelid.
explanation.definitionFit: Small inflamed bumps on the eyelid are literally sores of the eye.

clue.text: Left without restraint

explanation.surface: Someone departed with no holding back.
explanation.definitionFit: Deserted describes something left behind; unrestrained conduct is wild or uninhibited.

clue.text: Peter's minimal requirement? Jacket being worn

parts.note: a doublet is a close-fitting man's jacket of Tudor times
clothes being worn are on

explanation.surface: Peter needs very little: a jacket to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, to peter is to signal by playing a higher card then a lower one in a suit, which needs at least two cards: a holding of exactly two.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridge holding of just two cards in a suit, the least that allows a high-low signal.

clue.text: One who runs down side's right-half with vehicle

indicators.note: right-half takes the latter half of the word side, its right-hand two letters

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
a tractor is a farm vehicle

explanation.surface: A footballer playing right-half for a team drives a vehicle down someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right-half' looks like a football position but takes DE, the right-hand half of SIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A critic who belittles or disparages others is a person who knocks them.

clue.text: Architect, and rotter of the first water

parts.note: Robert Adam was a celebrated Scottish architect of the eighteenth century
a swine is a contemptible person, a rotter

explanation.surface: An architect and a scoundrel are both described as top quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of the first water' is a phrase meaning finest quality, but here it means water belonging to the first man, Adam: the jocular name for water.
explanation.definitionFit: Water, the only drink of the first man in Eden, is jokingly called his wine.

clue.text: As old as Iago was

explanation.surface: The character from Shakespeare was as aged as this.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Iago is called Othello's ancient, an old military rank equal to ensign.
explanation.definitionFit: Very old means aged; in Othello, Iago holds the rank of ancient, an old word for ensign or standard-bearer.

clue.text: Not censored, though such a book may be unreadable

definitions.text: such a book may be unreadable

explanation.surface: A book escaped the censor, though it may be too dense to read.
explanation.definitionFit: A film or text left whole has had nothing removed; an old book with untrimmed folded pages cannot be opened to read until they are slit.

clue.text: Up-to-date kennel fee?

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog, the kind that lives in a kennel
rent is the fee paid for accommodation

explanation.surface: A dog's lodging charge is fully paid up.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading: rent paid for a cur in its kennel.
explanation.definitionFit: Something present-day or in use now is modern and fresh.

clue.text: Thus I return to arrest islander

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, used to mark a quoted error

indicators.note: return tells the solver the word for arrest is turned to read backwards

parts.note: to nail a criminal is to arrest him

explanation.surface: Someone decides to come back and detain a man from an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses NAIL to give LIAN after SIC and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Mediterranean's largest island, home of Palermo.

clue.text: Fight in ring following Scottish pattern

indicators.note: following puts the ring's letter after the tartan word

parts.note: a sett is the pattern of a Scottish tartan
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A boxing bout in the ring follows the Scottish style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' puts O after SETT; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief fierce quarrel or bout of fisticuffs.

clue.text: Covering everything up in South ' America, it's plain

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the two words together are read from bottom to top

parts.note: on means covering, as a lid is on a jar
all means everything

explanation.surface: Someone hides everything in South America, and it's obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses ON ALL as one run, giving the letters backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A vast treeless grassy plain of northern South America, especially in Venezuela.

clue.text: Name for a girl — nothing odd in that

annotationWithheld.why: Name for a girl — nothing odd in that (6): GLORIA; the scan confirms the text, but no parse of 'nothing odd in that' gives GLORIA, and a search found no explanation.
annotationWithheld.clue: Name for a girl — nothing odd in that

clue.text: Check front of ship

explanation.surface: Inspect the bows of the vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem a flow is to stop it; the bow timber of a vessel is its forward post.

clue.text: The blame is meant ultimately for the medical worker

parts.note: to take the rap is to take the blame

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of meant

explanation.surface: Blame was intended, in the end, for a member of the medical staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes T, the last letter of meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A practitioner who treats illness or disorders by physical or psychological methods.

clue.text: It comes as a delightful surprise to doctor

definitions.text: It comes as a delightful surprise

explanation.surface: A physician receives an unexpected pleasant gift.
explanation.definitionFit: An unexpected pleasure is a special indulgence; doctors attend to patients medically.

clue.text: Isolated soldiers in mail? Just the reverse

parts.note: the opposite of the clue's in is out, so the phrase swaps one for the other
mail is the post

explanation.surface: Lonely troops wait for letters, or perhaps it is the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in mail' would be IN POST; 'Just the reverse' swaps IN for its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: A remote military station or the troops stationed there, far from the main force.

clue.text: German city's Irish quarter, roughly speaking

definitions.meaning: the 's stands for is: the city of Westphalia is the answer
one of Ireland's four provinces, roughly a quarter of the island

explanation.surface: A district of a German town is home to Irish people.
explanation.definitionFit: Münster is a cathedral city in Westphalia; the southern Irish province is one of four, so loosely a quarter of the country.
